title: Facile isolation of high-affinity nanobodies from synthetic libraries using CDR-swapping mutagenesis
protocol: Thaw a frozen aliquot of the nanobody yeast library on the benchtop at room temperature.
Add thawed yeast cells to 500 mL of SDCAA media in a baffled flask.
Supplement SDCAA media with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Incubate the flask at 30°C at 225 RPM for 18–24 h.
Calculate the cell density by measuring the optical density at 600 nm (OD600).
Calculate the volume of cells required to seed a 500 mL SDGCAA culture at a final OD600 of 1.
Centrifuge the required number of cells at 2500×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the cells in SDGCAA.
Move the cells to a 500 mL SDGCAA culture in a shake baffled flask.
Supplement SDGCAA media with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Incubate the flask at 20°C at 225 RPM for 36–48 h.
Calculate the OD600 of the SDGCAA culture.
Transfer volume corresponding to 10^9 cells to a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500×g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells by resuspending in 25 mL PBSB.
Repeat Steps 9 and 10.
Prepare 10% w/v milk solution in PBSB by dissolving 500 mg non-fat dry milk in 4.5 mL PBSB followed by end-over-end mixing at room temperature for 10-15 min.
Spin down milk solution at 2500×g for 5 min (room temperature).
Move the supernatant to a new tube.
Resuspend the cells in a final volume of 5 mL with 1% milk and 300 nM biotinylated monovalent antigen.
Incubate cells with antigen for 3 h at room temperature with end-over-end mixing.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500xg for 5 min.
Wash the cells once by resuspending in 25 mL ice-cold PBSB and centrifuge at 2500×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 40 mL ice-cold PBSB.
Add 750 μL Miltenyi MACS Streptavidin MicroBeads to the resuspended cells.
Incubate the cells and beads with end-over-end mixing at 4°C for 30–45 min.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500xg for 5 min.
Wash the cells once by resuspending in 25 mL ice-cold PBSB and centrifuge at 2500×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Pass the cells through a LS column under a magnetic field placed on a magnetic adapter.
Wash captured beads once by passing 5 mL ice-cold PBSB through the LS column under a magnetic field.
Remove the LS column from the magnet.
Elute beads by passing 5 mL SDCAA through the column.
Transfer eluted beads and cells to a 50 mL SDCAA media.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL kanamycin.
Add 0.01× Pen-strep to the culture.
Plate dilutions of the cell culture on yeast dropout plates to evaluate cell numbers retained during selection.
Grow cells in SDCAA culture and on dropout plates at 30°C for 2 days at 225 RPM.
Refresh cells stored at 4°C in fresh SDCAA for 18–24 hours prior to induction in SDGCAA.
Induce yeast cells collected in sort 1 in SDGCAA media as described in steps 3-6.
Culture volume may be decreased to 5–8 mL.
Calculate the OD600 of the SDGCAA culture.
Transfer volume corresponding to 107–108 yeast cells to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature).
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of PBSB.
Repeat Steps 30 and 31.
Incubate the resuspended cells with antigen and mouse anti-Myc tag antibody.
Mix ∼100–1000 nM antigen, cell solution, and diluted antibody to a final volume of 200 μL in a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 3 h with end-over-end mixing.
Include a control sample containing cells and all reagents except for the antigen.
Reduce the antigen concentration in progressive rounds of sorting to separate nanobodies with higher affinities.
Prepare samples at two different concentrations for sorting.
In cases where enrichment for clones binding to the antigen is modest, prepare samples at the same antigen concentration and three-fold dilution compared to the previous round.
For rapid progression in enrichment between rounds, prepare samples with three-fold and 10-fold reductions in antigen concentration from the previous round.
Collect cells from the lower of two examined antigen concentrations that shows a distinct binding population for efficient isolation of nanobodies with increased affinity.
Optional: Add milk to achieve a final concentration of 1% milk.
Post primary incubation, centrifuge the cells at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Wash the cells once by resuspending them in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the cells at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in ice-cold secondary labeling reagents and incubate on ice for 4 min.
Prepare secondary labeling solution in ice-cold PBSB.
Add a 1:200 dilution of goat anti-mouse IgG AlexaFluor 488 for detection of nanobody expression on yeast surface.
Dilute goat anti-human Fc IgG AlexaFluor 647 at a ratio of 1:300 for detection of antigen binding.
Dilute streptavidin AlexaFluor 647 at a ratio of 1:1000 for detection of monovalent biotinylated antigen binding.
Centrifuge cells at 16,000xg for 1 minute (room temperature) after secondary incubation.
Wash the cells once by resuspending them in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB.
Discard supernatant and place cells on ice.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB immediately before sorting to prevent dissociation of nanobody-antigen binding.
Sort the cells using a cell sorter under sterile conditions.
Examine forward scatter (FSC) and side scatter (SSC) of yeast cells with the 488 nm laser.
Adjust FSC and SSC voltages such that the population of cells spreads out in a diagonal line.
Draw a gate surrounding the main population of cells in the plot of FSC versus SSC such that events in the bottom left-hand corner (dead cells and debris) are not included.
Filter cells from within the gate on the FSC versus SSC plot into a subplot.
Examine the log area of signal from the fluorophore used to detect nanobody expression on the x-axis and the log area of the signal for the fluorophore used to detect antigen binding on the y-axis.
Analyze a control sample labeled with primary and secondary antibodies for detecting nanobody expression as well as secondary reagent for detecting antigen binding.
Adjust voltages for lasers exciting the fluorophores for detecting nanobody expression and antigen binding.
Adjust the voltage for the laser used for detecting nanobody expression such that two distinct cell populations are observed.
Draw quadrants to guide distinguishing the nanobody non-expressing and expressing cells.
Adjust the voltage for the laser used for detecting antigen binding such that signal from this laser is minimal in the control sample.
Ensure the signal is spaced away from the cytogram axis.
Adjust voltage and quadrants such that minimal signal is seen in the upper two quadrants.
Analyze positive samples to assess both nanobody expression and antigen binding.
Incubate cells with antigen at desired concentrations.
Label samples with secondary reagent for detecting bound antigen.
Label samples with primary and secondary reagents for detecting antibody expression.
Draw a gate in the upper right-hand quadrant of the cytogram.
Ensure the gate minimizes the number of cells present in the control sample.
Sort cells and transfer into an 8 mL SDCAA culture.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Grow cells in SDCAA culture at 30°C at 225 RPM for 2 days.
Refresh cells in fresh SDCAA for 18–24 hours prior to induction in SDGCAA after storing at 4°C.
Isolate plasmid DNA from the enriched library.
Obtain 1 mL of the 8 mL SDCAA culture collected in final FACS sort prior to CDR-swapping mutagenesis.
Recover nanobody library plasmids from 1 mL of sorted cells using a Zymo Yeast Miniprep Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Amplify individual CDR genes by mixing DNA isolated with Q5 DNA polymerase and associated reagents.
Amplify DNA segment including CDR1 (N-terminal homology-framework 1 to framework 2) using Forward primer #1 and Reverse primer #1.
Amplify DNA segment including CDR2 (framework 2 to framework 3) using Forward primer #2 and Reverse primer #2.
Amplify DNA segment including CDR3 using Forward primer #3 and Reverse primer #3.
Place PCR tubes in a PCR block with a heated lid.
Run PCR according to the specified conditions.
Store PCR products at 4°C overnight (∼12–24 h).
Separate the PCR product using a 1% agarose gel.
Cut DNA bands corresponding to ∼190–200 bp for CDR1 amplification.
Cut DNA bands corresponding to ∼160–170 bp for CDR2 amplification.
Cut DNA bands corresponding to ∼200–210 bp for CDR3 amplification.
Store agarose gel pieces containing amplified DNA at 4°C overnight (∼12–24 h).
Isolate DNA segments using a Qiagen Gel Extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Store isolated DNA at −20°C.
Mix amplified PCR products corresponding to each CDR gene in equal mass ratio.
Add terminal primers, Q5 polymerase, and reagents to the mixture.
Place the PCR tube in a PCR block with a heated lid.
Run PCR at the same conditions as Step 56.
Perform sufficient replicates (16–32 of the above described 50 μL PCR reactions) to generate 12 μg of insert DNA.
Store PCRs at 4°C overnight (∼12–24 h).
Purify the PCR product by separation using a 1% agarose gel.
Cut the DNA band at the expected size (∼520 base pairs for the given primers).
Isolate insert DNA using a Qiagen Gel Extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Incubate vector with NheI-HF and XhoI restriction enzymes at 37°C overnight.
Add Quick CIP to the restriction digest reaction and incubate at 37°C for at least 15 minutes.
Purify the digested vector by separating it using a 1% agarose gel.
Isolate the digested vector DNA using a Qiagen Gel Extraction kit.
Store the isolated digested vector DNA frozen at -20°C until use.
Mix 12 μg of insert DNA with 4 μg linearized plasmid.
Ethanol precipitate DNA with Pellet Paint NF Co-precipitant according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Cover ethanol precipitated DNA with aluminum foil and allow to dry completely overnight in a vacuum or chemical fume hood at room temperature.
Start a 5 mL culture of EBY100 yeast cells two days before transforming the library.
Grow the EBY100 yeast cell culture overnight (∼12–18 h) at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM.
Supplement the culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Seed a 50 mL culture of EBY100 yeast cells from the 5 mL culture started the previous day one day before transforming the library.
Grow the seeded culture overnight (∼12–24 h) at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM.
Supplement the seeded culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Inoculate a culture of EBY100 yeast cells from the 50 mL culture started the previous day.
Supplement the culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Grow cells at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM until an OD600 of ∼1.6 is reached.
Transfer 50 mL of the EBY100 culture to a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 25 mL sterile ice-cold DI water.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 25 mL sterile ice-cold electroporation buffer.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 25 mL sterile ice-cold conditioning buffer.
Incubate the cells at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM for 15 min.
Transfer 25 mL of cells in conditioning buffer to 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in ice-cold electroporation buffer to a final volume of 400 μL.
Add approximately 100–200 μL of electroporation buffer to achieve the final volume.
Resuspend ethanol precipitated DNA in prepared cells and electroporation buffer.
Transfer cells to a 2 mm electroporation cuvette and place on ice for 5 min.
Electroporate cells using an appropriate electroporator with settings: voltage 2500 V, resistance 200 Ω, capacitance 25 μF.
Immediately add 1 ml of a 1:1 mixture of YPD and 1 M sorbitol to the cells.
Transfer cells to a 14 mL culture tube and add 1:1 YPD:sorbitol to achieve a final volume of 8 mL.
Incubate cells at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM for 1 hour.
Centrifuge cells at 2500×g for 5 min (room temperature) and discard the supernatant.
Transfer cells to 200 ml of SDCAA.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/ml ampicillin, 100 μg/ml kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Plate dilutions of cell culture on yeast dropout plates to evaluate the number of transformants.
Grow cells in SDCAA and dropout plates at 30°C with agitation at 225 RPM for 2 days.
Refresh library in SDCAA for 18–24 hours prior to induction in SDGCAA after storing at 4°C.
For long-term storage, freeze the library at -80°C in a solution of 30% glycerol and 0.67% yeast nitrogen base (without amino acids).
Induce the CDR-swapped library in 200 mL SDGCAA media.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Calculate the OD600 of the SDGCAA culture.
Transfer volume corresponding to 10^7 yeast cells to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL PBSB.
Repeat steps of transferring volume corresponding to 10^7 yeast cells to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Incubate the cells with the desired concentration of antigen.
Resuspend antigen and cell solution in a final volume of 200 μL in a sterile 1.5 mL tube with a 1:1000 dilution of mouse anti-Myc tag antibody.
Incubate with antigen at room temperature for 3 h with end-over-end mixing.
Post primary incubation, centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min and discard supernatant.
Wash the cells once by resuspending them in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in ice-cold secondary labeling reagents and incubate on ice for 4 min.
Prepare secondary labeling solution in ice-cold PBSB.
Add a 1:200 dilution of goat anti-mouse IgG AlexaFluor 488 to the solution.
For monovalent biotinylated antigen, add a 1:1000 dilution of streptavidin AlexaFluor 647 for detection of antigen binding.
Post-secondary incubation, centrifuge the cells at 16,000xg for 1 min.
Wash the cells once by resuspending in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature) and discard supernatant.
Place cells on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL ice-cold PBSB immediately before loading into a cell sorter.
Sort the cells as described in Steps 43–52.
Obtain 1 mL of the 8 mL SDCAA culture collected in the final FACS sort (after CDR shuffling).
Recover nanobody library plasmids from 1 mL of sorted cells using a Zymo Yeast Miniprep Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Start a 5 mL culture of EBY100 cells containing individual nanobody plasmids isolated from the terminal selection using CDR-swapping mutagenesis in SDCAA.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Incubate yeast cells displaying nanobodies selected from the final round of sorting with a range of antigen concentrations.
Measure binding signals using flow cytometry.
Fit binding curves to the data in order to calculate dissociation constants for monovalent nanobodies.
Incubate the culture at 30°C at 225 RPM for 18–24 h.
Measure the OD600 of the SDCAA culture.
Calculate the volume of cells required to seed a 5 mL SDGCAA culture at a final OD600 of 1.
Centrifuge the corresponding volume of cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C).
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in SDGCAA.
Move the cells to a 5 mL SDGCAA culture.
Supplement culture with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, 100 μg/mL kanamycin, and 0.01× Pen-strep.
Incubate the culture at 20°C at 225 RPM for 36–48 h.
Measure the OD600 of the SDCAA culture.
Calculate the volume of cells required to obtain 1 × 10^5 yeast cells per antigen concentration to be examined.
Centrifuge the cells in a tabletop centrifuge at 16,000×g for 1 min (room temperature).
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL PBSB.
Repeat Steps 121 and 122 once.
Prepare antigen dilutions in PBSB with a final concentration of 1% milk in individual wells of a 96-well plate.
Add 1:1000 mouse anti-Myc antibody to each well containing antigen.
Add 1 × 10^5 cells to each well containing antigen.
Incubate at 350 RPM at room temperature for 3 h.
Centrifuge the plate containing the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C).
Discard supernatant.
Wash the cells once by resuspending them in 200 μL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the plate containing the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C).
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in ice-cold secondary labeling reagents.
Incubate on ice for 4 min.
Prepare secondary labeling solution in ice-cold PBSB.
Add 1:200 dilution of goat anti-mouse IgG AlexaFluor 488 to the solution.
For a monovalent biotinylated antigen, add 1:1000 dilution of streptavidin AlexaFluor 647 to the solution.
Centrifuge the plate containing the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C).
Discard supernatant.
Wash the cells once by resuspending them in 200 μL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the plate containing the cells at 2500×g for 5 min (4°C).
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in ice-cold PBSB.
Analyze the antigen binding signal of yeast cells expressing nanobodies on the surface by flow cytometry.
Purify DNA using a Qiagen Gel Extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Digest purified insert with NheI-HF and HindIII-HF according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Digest pTT5 vector with NheI-HF and HindIII-HF according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Add Quick CIP calf alkaline phosphatase to the vector reaction according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Purify the digested insert using a Qiagen PCR Purification kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Run the digested vector on a 1% agarose gel.
Purify DNA from the agarose gel using a Qiagen Gel Extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Ligate digested insert and linearized backbone with T4 ligase according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Transform the ligated plasmids into competent DH5α cells.
Plate transformed cells on LB ampicillin plates.
Grow plated cells at 37°C for 18–20 hours.
Pick individual colonies from the plates.
Grow picked colonies in LB media supplemented with 100 μg/mL ampicillin overnight (∼18–24 h) at 37°C.
Isolate plasmids from DH5α using a Qiagen Miniprep kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Confirm plasmid sequence via Sanger sequencing.
Grow HEK293-6E cells in supplemented F17 media at 37°C with 5% CO2 and mild agitation.
Maintain and passage cells at a density of ∼1.8–2 million cells/mL.
Transfect cells with 15 μg of sequence confirmed nanobody Fc-fusion.
Mix 15 μg plasmid, 45 μg PEI, and 3 mL un-supplemented F17 media and incubate at room temperature for 15–20 min.
Add prepared plasmid mixture to cells in culture tubes containing ∼25 mL cell culture.
Add 750 μL of 20% w/v yeastolate to the culture 24–48 h post transfection.
Grow cells for another 3–5 days at 37°C with 5% CO2 and mild agitation.
Centrifuge the cell cultures at 3500×g for 40 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube and add ∼0.5 mL Protein A agarose beads.
Incubate the supernatant and beads at 4°C overnight with mild agitation.
Capture beads in filter columns under vacuum.
Wash beads with approximately 50 mL of PBS.
Incubate beads with 0.1 M glycine (pH 3.0) for 15 minutes to elute protein solution.
Collect eluted protein solution by centrifugation.
Buffer exchange proteins into 20 mM acetate (pH 5.0) using Zeba desalting columns as per manufacturer’s protocol.
Filter nanobody Fc-fusions through a 0.22 μm filter.
Aliquot filtered nanobody Fc-fusions and store at -80°C until use.
Determine protein concentrations by measuring absorbance at 280 nm using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
Measure the purity of proteins using SDS-PAGE.
Prepare 1 × 10^5 antigen-coated beads per sample to be examined.
Transfer beads to a 1.5 mL tube and place on DynaMag™-2 Magnet.
Discard liquid after placing tubes on magnet.
Wash beads by resuspending in 1 mL of PBSB.
Place tube containing beads on magnet for 2–3 minutes.
Discard liquid from tube.
Repeat sub steps c and d.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL of 10% milk.
Mix resuspended beads for 1 hour with end-over-end mixing.
Place tube containing beads on the magnet.
Discard liquid from tube.
Wash beads by resuspending them in 1 mL of PBSB.
Place tube containing beads on the magnet for 2–3 minutes.
Discard liquid from tube.
Resuspend beads in PBSB (0.1–1 mL).
Thaw an aliquot of nanobody-Fc fusion protein.
Centrifuge nanobody-Fc fusion in a tabletop centrifuge at max speed for 5 minutes.
Transfer supernatant to a fresh tube.
Measure A280 signal for each nanobody using a Nanodrop to determine the protein concentration.
Prepare dilutions of nanobody-Fc fusion proteins in PBSB supplemented with 1% milk at concentrations (e.g., 0.1–1000 nM) desired for analysis.
Add 1 × 10^5 antigen-coated beads to antibody dilutions in each well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate soluble nanobody-Fc fusions and beads at 350 RPM and room temperature for 3 hours in a final volume of 200 μL.
Centrifuge the plate containing the beads at 2500×g for 5 minutes (4°C).
Discard supernatant from plate.
Wash beads once by resuspending them in 200 μL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the plate containing the beads at 2500×g for 5 minutes (4°C).
Discard supernatant from plate.
Resuspend the beads in 200 μL ice-cold secondary labeling reagents.
Incubate on ice for 4 min.
Prepare a secondary labeling solution in ice-cold PBSB at a 1:300 dilution (final concentration of ∼5 μg/mL) of goat anti-human IgG AlexaFluor 647 for detecting antigen binding.
Centrifuge the plate containing the beads at 2500×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the beads once by resuspending them in 200 μL ice-cold PBSB.
Centrifuge the plate containing the beads at 2500×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in ice-cold PBSB.
Analyze immediately by flow cytometry.
Analyze the antigen-binding signal of the singlet population of beads.
